name: CelesTrak Reference Nodes
description: Request-builder and parser flow nodes for the CelesTrak reference lanes: gp_groups turns a timer tick into one hostcap/http-request frame per GP group query (47 GROUP tokens plus the gpz / gpz-plus SPECIAL queries, overridable via node CONFIG celestrak_gp_groups) and ONE job frame carrying the ordered group list; parse_gp_groups pairs the responses with that list by ordinal and emits one $EGP (Entity Group, QUERY_SNAPSHOT membership over the group's OMM rows) per group, with the concatenated payloads as the raw archive and an 'unchanged' frame for groups that answered 304. satcat_reference emits the launch-site and owner/source table fetches; parse_satcat_reference reads those HTML tables into $SIT rows (launch sites) and $LCC rows (legacy owner codes, matched strictly against the generated enum; unknown codes become provenance warnings and are skipped). Every job carries origin_id celestrak.org, origin_name CelesTrak, dataset_id and the licence terms (node CONFIG celestrak_license / celestrak_license_url / celestrak_citation override the defaults), and every ingest meta carries the same attribution plus the wasm-authored provenance JSON. The job is one frame for all groups because the compiled flow runtime hands a node at most 64 frames per invocation; the group list is capped at 63 for the same reason. No capabilities: plugin.getConfig is a builtin and this module performs no I/O of its own.

sequentialJustification.detail: Every method is a single pass over the frames of one invocation: the request builders read the node config once and emit request and job frames; the parsers decode each response once into records. There is no shared mutable state, no worker pool and no fan-out inside the guest; the fan-out across group queries is the flow's, through the http connector node. This guest can never spawn a thread, so it compiles single-thread rather than claiming a wasi-threads contract it does not honour.

methods.description: Reads the single job frame and every response frame; response ordinal i is group i of the job list. The batch is refused (group-count-mismatch) when the counts differ and (group-url-mismatch) when a response names a different request URL. A group answering 304 is reported on 'unchanged'; any other non-200 status fails the batch, matching the CelesTrak usage policy. Each $EGP carries GROUP_ID celestrak.org/gp/<token>, sorted and deduplicated TAGS, QUERY_SNAPSHOT membership with one member per OMM row ($OMM, OBJECT_ID, NORAD_CAT_ID), the query URL, and provenance with the group payload's sha256 and the licence terms.

methods.description: Scans the page's first HTML table (tags stripped, entities decoded) and emits $SIT rows (ID and ABBREVIATION = the code, NAME and DESCRIPTION = the table description, SITE_TYPE LAUNCH_SITE, SOURCE CelesTrak) for dataset satcat-launch-sites, or $LCC rows (OWNER matched exactly against the generated legacyCountryCode labels, NAME/DESCRIPTION, ACTIVE, SOURCE_URL, RETRIEVED_AT from the response Date header) for dataset satcat-owners. An owner code absent from the enum is recorded as a provenance warning and skipped, never remapped. Every input port is single-stream; a surplus is refused (batched-input-frames).
